overview: This bill, called the REUSE Act, directs the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to study systems that let products and drink containers be refilled or reused many times instead of thrown away. Within two years, the EPA would publish a report on how practical these systems are and the best ways to run them in areas like restaurants and food service, groceries and beverages, cleaning and personal-care products, shipping, and schools and colleges. The report would look at job opportunities, costs and benefits for businesses and waste collectors, what kinds of government support would help, and what barriers stand in the way. The EPA would draw on programs in states, cities and other countries and consult with people involved in reuse and refill efforts. The Senate passed it, and as of November 20, 2025, it was being held at the House desk awaiting action.
for: Supporters say the report would give businesses and governments practical, evidence-based guidance on cutting waste and single-use packaging, without imposing any new mandates.
against: Critics say a federal study adds little that businesses and states are not already learning on their own, and could become a first step toward future packaging rules.
